root_cause: The header component incorrectly determines initial menu visibility by only checking for the 'govuk-header__navigation--open' class. On desktop, the menu is visible by default (without this class) while the menu button is hidden, but the component sets aria-expanded=true on the hidden button and aria-hidden=true on the visible menu.
repair_strategy: In the init method, detect whether the menu button is rendered (mobile) or hidden (desktop) using offsetParent. Compute menu visibility and button expanded state separately: menu is visible on desktop or when open on mobile; button is expanded only on mobile when menu is open. Set aria-expanded on button and aria-hidden on menu accordingly.
expected_accessibility_effect: On desktop, the navigation menu will have aria-hidden="false" and the menu button will have aria-expanded="false", exposing the navigation links to assistive technology. On mobile, the menu button will correctly reflect the menu state.
functional_risks: If the menu button's display property changes for reasons other than viewport width, visibility detection may be incorrect.
Future CSS changes affecting the button's layout could break the offsetParent check.
The component relies on the 'govuk-header__navigation--open' class for mobile menu state; ensuring that class toggling remains correct is essential.
verification_requirements: On desktop width, verify that the navigation menu has aria-hidden="false" and the menu button has aria-expanded="false".
On mobile width, verify that clicking the menu button toggles the open class, aria-expanded, and aria-hidden appropriately.
Confirm that Tab navigation reaches the #nav-apply element with role="link" and name="Apply" in both viewport states.
Ensure that the menu button remains functional for showing/hiding the menu on mobile.
